senses.gloss:
Chinnamastā
(‘one with a severed head’)
------------------------------------------
The तन्त्रस्, religio-philosophical texts devoted to the cult of worship of God as the Divine मोथेर्, speak of ten aspects of शक्ति (power of God, deified as his female consort) called ‘Daśamahā-विद्यास्’. Out of these ten, ‘Chinnamastā’ is the sixth in the series.
She is generally depicted as a goddess holding her own severed head in hand, which drinks the blood gushing out of her own body. She represents the continued state of self-sustenance of the created world in which are seen continuous self-destruction and self-renewal, in a cyclic order.
The Buddhist tāntrik goddess Vajrayoginī is iconographically similar to छिन्नमस्ता.
See DAŚAMAHĀVIDYĀS and TANTRAS.
